- **`Theorems.Normative.AuthzDecide.engine_catalogue_is_read_by_every_role`** — `GET /api/engines` (ENG-02c, #319) is read by every one of §21's four roles and written by none of the three narrower ones, whatever ownership the handler reports. The ownership quantifier is the point rather than a flourish. The catalogue is deployment configuration: it names no row, so the handler always answers `not-applicable`, and a grant of `any` is what makes that answer irrelevant — a reader gets the same decision for every ownership the handler could conceivably produce. `write: none` for admin, builder and viewer says the other half: an engine is installed by deploying an adapter, and no route writes one. Owner keeps §21's `Everything.` fallback and is therefore deliberately absent from the write half.

- **`Theorems.Normative.AuthzTenancy.authorise_follows_decide_after_an_ownership`** — When the resolver answers an ownership, `authorise` follows `decide()`: allow runs the handler with that ownership, deny is `403` with the decision's code (`token_out_of_scope` for a scope denial, otherwise `forbidden`), and refuse is `500 authorisation_undecidable` — a deny is never turned into a `404`.

- **`Theorems.Normative.ConceptIdentity.presented_bearers_follow_the_credential_table`** — "`Authorization: Bearer ak_live_<22>_<43>`" and "`awt_live_<22>_<43>`": the key grammar is the prefix `ak_live_`, a 22-character public half and a 43-character secret half; the browser-token grammar is the same with the prefix `awt_live_`; and each accepts exactly those half lengths.

- **`Theorems.Normative.ConceptIdentity.principal_is_a_membership_or_an_api_key_never_a_bare_user`** — "A principal is … a membership … or an API key … Never a bare user": a principal row has no `user_id` column, its kind is one of the two sources, and every source is one of the two kinds.

- **`Theorems.Normative.ConceptPublication.agent_share_defaults_to_definition`** — "Definition sharing is the default": an admitted agent share published without a mode is a `definition` share, and it carries no budget.
  - Statement: `∀ (r : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.PublishRequest) (role : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Membership.Role) (pse re : Bool) (now : Nat) (p : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.Published), r.subjectType = AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.SubjectType.agent → r.mode = none → AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.publishDecision r role pse re now = AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.PublishOutcome.published p → p.mode = some AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.Mode.definition ∧ p.budgetCapUsd = none`

- **`Theorems.Normative.ConceptPublication.budget_is_exhausted_at_the_cap`** — "Budget cap $20 total, then the link stops accepting messages": a runnable share whose spend has reached its cap is exhausted, and one below its cap is not.
  - Statement: `∀ (s : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Share.Share), s.budgetCapUsd = some "20" → (s.spentUsd = "20.000000" → s.budgetExhausted = true) ∧ (s.spentUsd = "19.999999" → s.budgetExhausted = false)`

- **`Theorems.Normative.ConceptWork.event_name_pattern_edges`** — `EVENT_NAME_PATTERN = /^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,63}$/` on its edges: a one-letter name and a 64-character name pass, a 65-character name fails, and a name that is empty, starts with a digit, `_`, `-` or `.`, or holds a space, `:` or a non-ASCII letter fails; every accepted name is at most 64 characters.
  - Statement: `AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RunEvent.isEventName "a" = true ∧ AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RunEvent.isEventName ("a" ++ String.ofList (List.replicate 63 '9')) = true ∧ AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RunEvent.isEventName ("a" ++ String.ofList (List.replicate 64 '9')) = false ∧ AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RunEvent.isEventName "Z.b_c-9" = true ∧ (["", "1abc", "_abc", "-abc", ".abc", "a b", "a:b", "é"].all fun x => !AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RunEvent.isEventName x) = true ∧ ∀ (s : String), AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RunEvent.isEventName s = true → s.length ≤ 64`
  - Cites: `packages/contracts/src/run-events.ts#EVENT_NAME_PATTERN`
- **`Theorems.Normative.ConceptWork.frame_kinds_are_disjoint_and_only_control_is_transient`** — Control frames "carry no `id:` and never move the resume cursor", while `run.status` and the relayed runtime events are durable; the three name lists are disjoint, so every listed name has exactly one kind.
  - Statement: `(AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RunEvent.controlFrameNames.all fun n => AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RunEvent.frameKind? n == some AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RunEvent.FrameKind.control) = true ∧ AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RunEvent.frameKind? AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RunEvent.runStatusEvent = some AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RunEvent.FrameKind.platform ∧ (AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RunEvent.relayedEventNames.all fun n => AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RunEvent.frameKind? n == some AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RunEvent.FrameKind.relayed) = true ∧ (AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RunEvent.controlFrameNames ++ AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RunEvent.runStatusEvent :: AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RunEvent.relayedEventNames).Nodup ∧ AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RunEvent.FrameKind.control.durable = false ∧ AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RunEvent.FrameKind.platform.durable = true ∧ AgentWorkspace.Concepts.RunEvent.FrameKind.relayed.durable = true`
  - Cites: `docs/sdk/site/concepts/run-lifecycle.mdx#the-event-stream`, `packages/contracts/src/run-events.ts#CONTROL_FRAME_NAMES`, `packages/contracts/src/run-events.ts#RELAYED_EVENT_NAMES`
- **`Theorems.Normative.ConceptWork.ledger_accounting_follows_the_priced_rows`** — The ledger's accounting state: no settlement is `pending`; after one, it is priced exactly when some ledger row is priced, `complete` when every row is and `unavailable` when none is.
  - Statement: `∀ (records : List AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Usage.UsageRecord), (records = [] → AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Usage.ledgerAccounting records = AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Usage.AccountingState.pending) ∧ (records ≠ [] → (AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Usage.ledgerAccounting records).isPriced = records.any AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Usage.UsageRecord.isPriced) ∧ (records ≠ [] → records.all AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Usage.UsageRecord.isPriced = true → AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Usage.ledgerAccounting records = AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Usage.AccountingState.complete) ∧ (records ≠ [] → (records.all fun x => !x.isPriced) = true → AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Usage.ledgerAccounting records = AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Usage.AccountingState.unavailable)`
  - Cites: `packages/core/src/db/repositories/runs.ts#pricedCount`, `packages/core/src/db/schema/runs.ts#accountingStates`

- **`Theorems.Normative.ConceptWork.main_transcript_has_no_wire_subpath`** — The main transcript is stored under the empty subpath, which the wire refuses as a subpath ("the empty string is refused rather than read as 'none'"), and every wire subpath is at most 128 characters.

- **`Theorems.Normative.ConceptWork.mixed_ledger_is_partial`** — A ledger with at least one priced and at least one unpriced row is `partial`: the run's cost is known for some of its responses but not all of them.

- **`Theorems.Normative.ConceptWork.negative_nonzero_decimal_is_refused`** — A leading `-` on a nonzero decimal is refused by the `≥ 0` half of the counter checks: the only negative-signed amount a run or a ledger row may carry is a spelling of zero.

- **`Theorems.Normative.ConceptWork.new_run_is_queued_unpriced_and_well_formed`** — A run exists as soon as it is started, as `queued` ("the run already exists, with `status: 'queued'`"), with zero usage, the zero cost `'0.000000'` in USD, no price table version and accounting `pending`, and it passes every check.

- **`Theorems.Normative.ConceptWork.project_list_filters_partition`** — The `?archived=` filters partition projects: every project is listed by exactly one of `active` and `archived`, and by `all`; its state is `archived` exactly when `archivedAt` is set.

- **`Theorems.Normative.ConceptWork.tenant_scope_accepts_a_workspace_key`** — With a non-blank configuration directory, the tenant session scope keyed by a workspace id is always accepted by `validateTenantSessionScope`.
  - Statement: `∀ (ws configDir : String), AgentWorkspace.Uuid.isCanonical ws = true → AgentWorkspace.Concepts.ModelConnection.isBlank configDir = false → AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Session.tenantScopeOk ws configDir = true`
  - Cites: `docs/formal/inventory.md#4-tenant-isolation-predicates`, `packages/run-protocol/src/schemas.ts#validateTenantSessionScope`
- **`Theorems.Normative.ConceptWork.tenant_scope_refusals`** — The refusals, by case: a device-name key (`con`, `COM1`, `lpt9`), an empty or 65-character key, a key with a `/` or `.`, and a blank configuration directory (ASCII blanks, or the Unicode blanks `String.prototype.trim` also strips: U+3000, U+2028, U+205F, U+1680, U+FEFF) are all refused, while a 64-character key under a real directory is accepted, and a directory holding a zero-width space (U+200B, not whitespace to ECMAScript) is not blank.
  - Statement: `(["con", "COM1", "lpt9", "", "a/b", "..", String.ofList (List.replicate 65 'k')].all fun k => !AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Session.tenantScopeOk k "/var/lib/aw") = true ∧ AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Session.tenantScopeOk "workspace-1" " \t\n" = false ∧ AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Session.tenantScopeOk "workspace-1" "" = false ∧ (["　", " ", " ", " ", "﻿", "   "].all fun d => !AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Session.tenantScopeOk "workspace-1" d) = true ∧ AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Session.tenantScopeOk "workspace-1" "​" = true ∧ AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Session.tenantScopeOk (String.ofList (List.replicate 64 'k')) "/var/lib/aw" = true`
  - Cites: `docs/formal/inventory.md#4-tenant-isolation-predicates`, `packages/run-protocol/src/schemas.ts#validateTenantSessionScope`
- **`Theorems.Normative.ConceptWork.tenant_scope_refuses_unsafe_keys`** — `validateTenantSessionScope` accepts only a scope the SDK keeps apart from every other: the key is one directory name of 1 to 64 characters with no path separator and no `.` (so no `..` and no hidden or relative path), it is not a Windows device name, and the configuration directory is not blank.
  - Statement: `∀ (k d : String), AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Session.tenantScopeOk k d = true → 1 ≤ k.length ∧ k.length ≤ 64 ∧ (∀ (c : Char), c ∈ k.toList → c ≠ '/' ∧ c ≠ '\\' ∧ c ≠ '.') ∧ AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Session.isWindowsDeviceName k = false ∧ AgentWorkspace.Concepts.ModelConnection.isBlank d = false`
  - Cites: `docs/formal/inventory.md#4-tenant-isolation-predicates`, `packages/run-protocol/src/schemas.ts#validateTenantSessionScope`, `packages/contracts/src/sessions.ts#PROJECT_KEY_PATTERN`
- **`Theorems.Normative.ConceptWork.total_tokens_is_the_sum_of_four_counters`** — `totalTokens` is "the sum of the four" token counters: it never counts tool calls, and it adds up across settlements (the total of a sum of counters is the sum of their totals).
  - Statement: `∀ (c d : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Usage.Counters), c.totalTokens = { inputTokens := c.inputTokens, outputTokens := c.outputTokens, cacheReadInputTokens := c.cacheReadInputTokens, cacheCreationInputTokens := c.cacheCreationInputTokens, toolCalls := 0 }.totalTokens ∧ (c.add d).totalTokens = c.totalTokens + d.totalTokens ∧ { inputTokens := 1, outputTokens := 2, cacheReadInputTokens := 4, cacheCreationInputTokens := 8, toolCalls := 16 }.totalTokens = 15`
  - Cites: `docs/sdk/site/concepts/run-lifecycle.mdx#usage-cost-and-accounting`, `packages/contracts/src/runs.ts#RunUsageSchema`

### T1 · ContractsEngines

- **`Theorems.Normative.ContractsEngines.a_capability_refusal_names_a_real_gap`** — When it refuses, the capability it names is one the engine really lacks **and** the agent really demands. A refusal never names a capability that is beside the point.
  - Statement: `(AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.assignmentCapabilities.all fun cap => AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.assignmentDemands.all fun demand => match AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.unsupportedCapability cap demand with | some AgentWorkspace.Contracts.Engines.CapabilityKey.mcp => demand.connectors && !cap.mcp | some AgentWorkspace.Contracts.Engines.CapabilityKey.skills => demand.skills && !cap.skills | some AgentWorkspace.Contracts.Engines.CapabilityKey.subagents => demand.subagents && !cap.subagents | none => true) = true`
  - Cites: `apps/web/server/engines/capabilities.ts#unsupportedEngineCapability`
- **`Theorems.Normative.ContractsEngines.a_refusal_only_names_a_published_capability`** — Every capability a refusal can name is one the published capability set has a field for, so a `details` entry always points at something an engine descriptor really states.
  - Statement: `AgentWorkspace.Contracts.Engines.capabilityKeys = ["mcp", "skills", "subagents"]`
  - Cites: `packages/contracts/src/engines.ts#ENGINE_CAPABILITY_KEYS`
- **`Theorems.Normative.ContractsEngines.a_registered_engine_reaches_the_union`** — The engine this deployment does register reaches the union, and the union's answer is the parser's answer. Nothing above turns a well-formed Claude policy into a refusal.
  - Statement: `AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.parsePolicy AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.defaultRegistered (fun x => true) AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ContractsEngines.claudeBody✝ = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.PolicyVerdict.accepted ∧ AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.parsePolicy AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.defaultRegistered (fun x => false) AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ContractsEngines.claudeBody✝ = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.PolicyVerdict.invalidPolicy`
  - Cites: `apps/web/server/agents/policy.ts#parsePolicyBody`
- **`Theorems.Normative.ContractsEngines.capability_check_refines_compose`** — The save-time check refines ENG-01's `compose`: it saves exactly when `compose` accepts. So the concrete refusal is the abstract rule instantiated, not a second rule that happens to resemble it.
  - Statement: `(AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.assignmentCapabilities.all fun cap => AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.assignmentDemands.all fun demand => (AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.saveAgent cap demand == AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.CapabilityVerdict.saved) == (AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Engine.compose (AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ContractsEngines.abstractAgent✝ demand) (AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ContractsEngines.abstractEngine✝ cap) == AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Engine.ComposeResult.accepted)) = true`
  - Cites: `docs/adr/0065-an-agents-engine-is-an-extension-point-behind-one-port.md#d3--what-the-platform-refuses-to-own`, `apps/web/server/agents/policy.ts#engineCapabilityRefusal`
- **`Theorems.Normative.ContractsEngines.capability_refusal_is_exact`** — The check refuses **exactly** the agents whose connectors, skills or subagents the engine cannot honour: no refusal precisely when every demanded resource is supported, and a refusal in every other case. Both directions, which is what rules out a check that is merely conservative.
  - Statement: `(AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.assignmentCapabilities.all fun cap => AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.assignmentDemands.all fun demand => (AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.unsupportedCapability cap demand).isNone == AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.honoursAssignments cap demand) = true`
  - Cites: `docs/adr/0065-an-agents-engine-is-an-extension-point-behind-one-port.md#d3--what-the-platform-refuses-to-own`, `apps/web/server/engines/capabilities.ts#unsupportedEngineCapability`
- **`Theorems.Normative.ContractsEngines.claude_agent_sdk_never_refuses_an_assignment`** — Nothing changes for `claude-agent-sdk`'s assignments. It honours both assignable resources, so the check never fires for it on connectors or skills, whatever the agent is assigned — which is why the refusal of an assignment needs a test-only descriptor to be reachable at all. A subagent is a different matter: like every catalogue engine it declares `subagents: false`, so a demand for one is refused naming `subagents`, whatever else the agent is assigned.
  - Statement: `(AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.assignmentDemands.all fun demand => AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.saveAgent AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.claudeAssignmentCapabilities demand == if demand.subagents = true then AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.CapabilityVerdict.unsupported AgentWorkspace.Contracts.Engines.CapabilityKey.subagents else AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.CapabilityVerdict.saved) = true`
  - Cites: `apps/web/server/engines/registry.ts#registeredEngines`
- **`Theorems.Normative.ContractsEngines.default_registry_is_the_catalogue`** — The registry a deployment installs by default is exactly the published catalogue.
  - Statement: `AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.defaultRegistered = AgentWorkspace.Contracts.Engines.engineIds`
  - Cites: `apps/web/server/engines/registry.ts#registeredEngines`
- **`Theorems.Normative.ContractsEngines.engine_capability_unsupported_is_a_four_twenty_two`** — The refusal travels as `422 engine_capability_unsupported`, and its `details` is exactly the capability — one published wire string, never prose a client would have to parse.
  - Statement: `(AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.CapabilityVerdict.unsupported AgentWorkspace.Contracts.Engines.CapabilityKey.mcp).code = some "engine_capability_unsupported" ∧ (AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.CapabilityVerdict.unsupported AgentWorkspace.Contracts.Engines.CapabilityKey.mcp).status = 422 ∧ (AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.CapabilityVerdict.unsupported AgentWorkspace.Contracts.Engines.CapabilityKey.mcp).details = ["mcp"] ∧ (AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.CapabilityVerdict.unsupported AgentWorkspace.Contracts.Engines.CapabilityKey.skills).details = ["skills"] ∧ (AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.CapabilityVerdict.unsupported AgentWorkspace.Contracts.Engines.CapabilityKey.subagents).details = ["subagents"] ∧ AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.CapabilityVerdict.saved.details = []`
  - Cites: `packages/contracts/src/engines.ts#ENGINE_PROBLEM_CODES`, `packages/contracts/src/engines.ts#ENGINE_CAPABILITY_KEYS`
- **`Theorems.Normative.ContractsEngines.legacy_provider_discriminant_is_always_refused`** — A body carrying `provider` and no `engine` is refused as `invalid_body`, whatever the union would have said about the rest of it. There is no silent acceptance of the old shape.
  - Statement: `(AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ContractsEngines.legacyBodies✝.all fun j => AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ContractsEngines.unionVerdicts✝.all fun accept => AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.parsePolicy AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.defaultRegistered accept j == AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.PolicyVerdict.invalidBody) = true`
  - Cites: `docs/adr/0065-an-agents-engine-is-an-extension-point-behind-one-port.md#d1--vocabulary`, `apps/web/server/agents/policy.ts#parsePolicyBody`
- **`Theorems.Normative.ContractsEngines.legacy_refusal_names_the_rename`** — The refusal carries `invalid_body` at `400`, not the union's `invalid_policy`: a client on the old shape is told about the rename rather than handed a list of complaints about a missing key.
  - Statement: `AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.PolicyVerdict.invalidBody.code = some "invalid_body" ∧ AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.PolicyVerdict.invalidBody.status = 400 ∧ AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.PolicyVerdict.invalidBody ≠ AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.PolicyVerdict.invalidPolicy`
  - Cites: `packages/contracts/src/agents.ts#AGENT_POLICY_PROBLEM_CODES`
- **`Theorems.Normative.ContractsEngines.naming_both_discriminants_is_refused`** — Naming **both** discriminants is refused too. The engine check passes — `claude-agent-sdk` is registered — and the union refuses the extra key, so the body reaches `invalid_policy` rather than being read as either shape.
  - Statement: `AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.parsePolicy AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.defaultRegistered (fun x => false) AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ContractsEngines.bothBody✝ = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.PolicyVerdict.invalidPolicy`
  - Cites: `packages/contracts/src/agents.ts#AgentPolicySchema`
- **`Theorems.Normative.ContractsEngines.the_refusal_is_about_the_registry`** — `unsupported_engine` is a statement about the **registry**, not about the spelling: registering acp moves the same body off that refusal and onto the union's own verdict.
  - Statement: `AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.parsePolicy AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.defaultRegistered (fun x => true) AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ContractsEngines.acpBody✝ = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.PolicyVerdict.unsupportedEngine ∧ AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.parsePolicy ["claude-agent-sdk", "acp"] (fun x => true) AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ContractsEngines.acpBody✝ = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.PolicyVerdict.accepted ∧ AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.parsePolicy ["claude-agent-sdk", "acp"] (fun x => false) AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ContractsEngines.acpBody✝ = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.PolicyVerdict.invalidPolicy`
  - Cites: `apps/web/server/engines/registry.ts#registeredEngineIds`
- **`Theorems.Normative.ContractsEngines.unregistered_engine_is_always_refused`** — An engine this deployment does not register is refused as `unsupported_engine`, whatever the union would have said. A body whose `engine` is not even a string is refused here too: it names an engine, and no registry contains it.
  - Statement: `(AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ContractsEngines.unregisteredBodies✝.all fun j => AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.ContractsEngines.unionVerdicts✝.all fun accept => AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.parsePolicy AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.defaultRegistered accept j == AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.PolicyVerdict.unsupportedEngine) = true`
  - Cites: `docs/adr/0065-an-agents-engine-is-an-extension-point-behind-one-port.md#d3--what-the-platform-refuses-to-own`, `apps/web/server/agents/policy.ts#parsePolicyBody`
- **`Theorems.Normative.ContractsEngines.unsupported_engine_is_a_four_hundred`** — The refusal carries `unsupported_engine` at `400`.
  - Statement: `AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.PolicyVerdict.unsupportedEngine.code = some "unsupported_engine" ∧ AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.PolicyVerdict.unsupportedEngine.status = 400`
  - Cites: `packages/contracts/src/engines.ts#ENGINE_PROBLEM_CODES`

### T1 · ContractsFoundation

- **`Theorems.Normative.ContractsFoundation.api_key_not_permitted_is_not_shared`** — `api_key_not_permitted` is not one of the shared codes: it belongs to the workspace and invitation routes.
  - Statement: `AgentWorkspace.WireEnum.ofWire? "api_key_not_permitted" = none`

- **`Theorems.Normative.ContractsFoundation.bare_message_defaults_to_empty`** — A bare envelope is read with its `message`, or `''` when the server sent none.
  - Statement: `∀ (b : AgentWorkspace.Contracts.Problem.ApiProblemBareCode), AgentWorkspace.Contracts.Problem.apiProblemBareCodeCodec.valid b = true → AgentWorkspace.Contracts.Problem.normaliseCurrent (AgentWorkspace.Contracts.Problem.apiProblemBareCodeCodec.encode b) = some { code := b.error, message := b.message.getD "", details := none }`
  - Cites: `docs/sdk/site/guides/errors.mdx#three-envelope-spellings-one-shape`, `packages/sdk/src/http.ts#readProblem`
- **`Theorems.Normative.ContractsFoundation.common_code_statuses_are_documented`** — Every shared code travels under a failure status SPEC §4 lists.
  - Statement: `∀ (c : AgentWorkspace.Contracts.Problem.CommonProblemCode), AgentWorkspace.Contracts.Problem.documentedFailureStatus c.status = true`
  - Cites: `docs/sdk/04-api-specification.md#4-conventions`, `packages/contracts/src/problem.ts#COMMON_PROBLEM_CODES`
- **`Theorems.Normative.ContractsFoundation.common_codes_match_errors_guide`** — The shared codes and their statuses are, row for row, the errors guide's table.
  - Statement: `List.map (fun c => (AgentWorkspace.WireEnum.toWire c, c.status)) AgentWorkspace.WireEnum.all = AgentWorkspace.Contracts.Problem.documentedCommonCodes`
  - Cites: `docs/sdk/site/guides/errors.mdx#common_problem_codes`, `packages/contracts/src/problem.ts#COMMON_PROBLEM_CODES`
- **`Theorems.Normative.ContractsFoundation.detail_becomes_message`** — An RBAC envelope is read with its `detail` as the `message`, and no details.
  - Statement: `∀ (d : AgentWorkspace.Contracts.Problem.ApiProblemDetail), AgentWorkspace.Contracts.Problem.apiProblemDetailCodec.valid d = true → AgentWorkspace.Contracts.Problem.normaliseCurrent (AgentWorkspace.Contracts.Problem.apiProblemDetailCodec.encode d) = some { code := d.code, message := d.detail, details := none }`

  - Statement: `∀ {r : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Request} {grants : List AgentWorkspace.Authz.PathGrant.Grant}, r.policyReadable = true → AgentWorkspace.Authz.PathGrant.normaliseGrants (some AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.protectedDirectory) r.grants = some grants → r.skills = [] → r.session = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.SessionMode.fork → AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.compile r = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Outcome.refused (AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Refusal.capabilityUnsupported "fork")`
  - Cites: `docs/formal/units/engine-openai-agents.md#compile`, `packages/engine-openai-agents/src/compile.ts#compileOpenAiAgentsRun`
- **`Theorems.Normative.OpenAiAgents.a_granted_skill_is_refused_by_name`** — A granted skill is refused `engine_capability_unsupported` naming `skills` (the engine declares `skills: false`), never dropped.
  - Statement: `∀ {r : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Request} {grants : List AgentWorkspace.Authz.PathGrant.Grant}, r.policyReadable = true → AgentWorkspace.Authz.PathGrant.normaliseGrants (some AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.protectedDirectory) r.grants = some grants → r.skills ≠ [] → AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.compile r = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Outcome.refused (AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Refusal.capabilityUnsupported "skills")`
  - Cites: `docs/formal/units/engine-openai-agents.md#compile`, `packages/engine-openai-agents/src/compile.ts#compileOpenAiAgentsRun`
- **`Theorems.Normative.OpenAiAgents.a_remote_connector_needs_no_network_switch`** — Remote MCP parity with the Claude engine (Owner decision on #308, ADR-0074 D2): a connector that asks for no approval is compiled whether it is remote or stdio, so `unrestrictedNetwork` off never removes an assigned remote connector.
  - Statement: `∀ (c : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Connector) (rest : List AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Connector), c.asksApproval = false → AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.compileConnectors (c :: rest) = Except.map (fun x => c.name :: x) (AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.compileConnectors rest)`
  - Cites: `docs/formal/units/engine-openai-agents.md#compile`, `packages/engine-openai-agents/src/compile.ts#compileOpenAiAgentsRun`
- **`Theorems.Normative.OpenAiAgents.accepted_agent_offers_exactly_the_permitted_tools`** — An accepted agent offers exactly the tools the four permission switches allow, with `shell` withheld while a read-only grant exists.
  - Statement: `∀ {r : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Request} {c : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Compiled}, AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.compile r = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Outcome.ok c → ∀ (t : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Tool), t ∈ c.tools ↔ AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Tool.permitted r.permissions t = true ∧ ¬(t = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Tool.shell ∧ (c.grants.any fun x => x.readOnly) = true)`
  - Cites: `docs/formal/units/engine-openai-agents.md#tools`, `packages/engine-openai-agents/src/tools.ts#openAiAgentsToolPlan`, `packages/engine-openai-agents/src/compile.ts#compileOpenAiAgentsRun`
- **`Theorems.Normative.OpenAiAgents.an_accepted_budget_cap_is_priced_and_compiled`** — Every accepted compile carries the request's cap into the configuration the boundary enforces it from, and a cap is only ever accepted on a model the provisional table prices: the cap is neither dropped nor accepted unenforceable (ADR-0074 D7).
  - Statement: `∀ {r : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Request} {c : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Compiled}, AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.compile r = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Outcome.ok c → c.budgetCap = r.budgetCap ∧ (r.budgetCap = true → AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.priced r.model = true)`
  - Cites: `docs/formal/units/engine-openai-agents.md#compile`, `packages/engine-openai-agents/src/compile.ts#compileOpenAiAgentsRun`
- **`Theorems.Normative.OpenAiAgents.an_unhonourable_connector_is_refused_by_name`** — A connector whose tool asks for a human approval is refused naming `approvals`; it is not silently left out.
  - Statement: `∀ (c : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Connector) (rest : List AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Connector), c.asksApproval = true → AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.compileConnectors (c :: rest) = Except.error (AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Refusal.capabilityUnsupported "approvals")`
  - Cites: `docs/formal/units/engine-openai-agents.md#compile`, `packages/engine-openai-agents/src/compile.ts#compileOpenAiAgentsRun`
- **`Theorems.Normative.OpenAiAgents.an_unpriced_budget_cap_is_refused_by_name`** — A per-run budget cap the provisional price table cannot price — an unlisted model, or none named — is refused naming `maxBudget`: a cap that could never stop the run is not accepted (ADR-0074 D7).
  - Statement: `∀ {r : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Request} {grants : List AgentWorkspace.Authz.PathGrant.Grant}, r.policyReadable = true → AgentWorkspace.Authz.PathGrant.normaliseGrants (some AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.protectedDirectory) r.grants = some grants → r.skills = [] → r.session ≠ AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.SessionMode.fork → r.budgetCap = true → AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.priced r.model = false → AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.compile r = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Outcome.refused (AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Refusal.capabilityUnsupported "maxBudget")`
  - Cites: `docs/formal/units/engine-openai-agents.md#compile`, `packages/engine-openai-agents/src/compile.ts#compileOpenAiAgentsRun`
- **`Theorems.Normative.OpenAiAgents.an_unspoken_protocol_is_refused_by_name`** — A protocol the engine does not speak is refused naming `wireProtocols`.
  - Statement: `∀ {r : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Request} {grants : List AgentWorkspace.Authz.PathGrant.Grant} {b t w : String}, r.policyReadable = true → AgentWorkspace.Authz.PathGrant.normaliseGrants (some AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.protectedDirectory) r.grants = some grants → r.skills = [] → r.session ≠ AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.SessionMode.fork → r.budgetCap = false → r.gateway = some (b, t, w) → AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Protocol.ofWire? w = none → AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.compile r = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Outcome.refused (AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Refusal.capabilityUnsupported "wireProtocols")`
  - Cites: `docs/formal/units/engine-openai-agents.md#compile`, `packages/engine-openai-agents/src/compile.ts#compileOpenAiAgentsRun`
- **`Theorems.Normative.OpenAiAgents.anthropic_without_a_model_is_refused_by_name`** — An Anthropic-family connection with no model named is refused naming `model`: the AI SDK adapter has no default model, and the adapter does not invent one.
  - Statement: `∀ {r : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Request} {grants : List AgentWorkspace.Authz.PathGrant.Grant} {b t : String}, r.policyReadable = true → AgentWorkspace.Authz.PathGrant.normaliseGrants (some AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.protectedDirectory) r.grants = some grants → r.skills = [] → r.session ≠ AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.SessionMode.fork → r.budgetCap = false → r.gateway = some (b, t, "anthropic-messages") → r.model = none → AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.compile r = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Outcome.refused (AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Refusal.capabilityUnsupported "model")`
  - Cites: `docs/formal/units/engine-openai-agents.md#compile`, `packages/engine-openai-agents/src/compile.ts#compileOpenAiAgentsRun`
- **`Theorems.Normative.OpenAiAgents.compiled_protocol_is_the_gateway_protocol`** — An accepted compile speaks exactly the protocol the gateway connection names, through the client that protocol selects.
  - Statement: `∀ {r : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Request} {c : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Compiled}, AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.compile r = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Outcome.ok c → ∃ b t w, r.gateway = some (b, t, w) ∧ c.connection.protocol.toWire = w ∧ c.connection.client = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.clientFor c.connection.protocol`
  - Cites: `docs/formal/units/engine-openai-agents.md#compile`, `packages/engine-openai-agents/src/compile.ts#compileOpenAiAgentsRun`
- **`Theorems.Normative.OpenAiAgents.no_vendor_hosted_tool_is_compiled`** — No compiled tool is vendor-hosted: every one is sent as a function tool, which the gateway's closed hosted-tool allowlist relays.
  - Statement: `∀ {r : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Request} {c : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Compiled}, AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.compile r = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Outcome.ok c → ∀ (t : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Tool), t ∈ c.tools → t.wireType = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.GatewayIngress.ToolType.function ∧ t.wireType.isRelayable = true`
  - Cites: `docs/formal/units/engine-openai-agents.md#tools`, `packages/engine-openai-agents/src/boundary.ts#startOpenAiAgentsRun`, `packages/gateway/src/providers/passthrough.ts#unrelayableToolType`
- **`Theorems.Normative.OpenAiAgents.the_protocol_follows_the_connection`** — Compose resolves an OpenAI-family connection to the Responses dialect and an Anthropic-family one to Messages for this engine, and the compiled client follows the protocol: `OpenAIProvider` for the two OpenAI dialects, `aisdk()` for Messages.
  - Statement: `(["openai", "azure-openai", "openai-compatible"].all fun provider => AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.EnginePort.resolveWireProtocol AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.engineProtocols provider == some "openai-responses") = true ∧ (["anthropic", "anthropic-compatible"].all fun provider => AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.EnginePort.resolveWireProtocol AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.engineProtocols provider == some "anthropic-messages") = true ∧ AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.clientFor AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Protocol.openaiResponses = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Client.openai ∧ AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.clientFor AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Protocol.openaiChatCompletions = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Client.openai ∧ AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.clientFor AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Protocol.anthropicMessages = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Client.aisdkAnthropic`
  - Cites: `docs/formal/units/engine-openai-agents.md#compile`, `apps/web/server/engines/protocol.ts#resolveWireProtocol`, `packages/engine-openai-agents/src/compile.ts#openAiAgentsModelConnection`
- **`Theorems.Normative.OpenAiAgents.the_sdk_shell_tool_type_is_not_relayed`** — Why the tools are function tools: the SDK's own `shell` tool type is one the gateway refuses as hosted, so an adapter that compiled it could not reach its model through the gateway.
  - Statement: `AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.GatewayIngress.ToolType.shell.isRelayable = false`
  - Cites: `docs/formal/units/engine-openai-agents.md#tools`, `packages/contracts/src/agents.ts#OPENAI_AGENTS_TOOL_NAMES`

### T1 · Pi

- **`Theorems.Normative.Pi.a_connector_is_refused_by_name`** — A connector is refused `engine_capability_unsupported` naming `mcp` on a request whose policy and grants read, never dropped and never bridged.
  - Statement: `∀ {r : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Pi.Request} {grants : List AgentWorkspace.Authz.PathGrant.Grant}, r.policyReadable = true → AgentWorkspace.Authz.PathGrant.normaliseGrants (some AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Pi.protectedDirectory) r.grants = some grants → r.connectors ≠ [] → AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Pi.compile r = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Pi.Outcome.refused (AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Refusal.capabilityUnsupported "mcp")`
  - Cites: `docs/formal/units/engine-pi.md#compile`, `packages/engine-pi/src/compile.ts#compilePiRun`
- **`Theorems.Normative.Pi.accepted_agent_offers_exactly_the_permitted_tools`** — An accepted agent offers exactly the tools the four permission switches allow, with `bash` withheld while a read-only grant exists.
  - Statement: `∀ {r : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Pi.Request} {c : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Pi.Compiled}, AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Pi.compile r = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Pi.Outcome.ok c → ∀ (t : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Pi.Tool), t ∈ c.tools ↔ AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Pi.Tool.permitted r.permissions t = true ∧ ¬(t = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Pi.Tool.bash ∧ (c.grants.any fun x => x.readOnly) = true)`
  - Cites: `docs/formal/units/engine-pi.md#tools`, `packages/engine-pi/src/tools.ts#piToolPlan`, `packages/engine-pi/src/compile.ts#compilePiRun`
- **`Theorems.Normative.Pi.an_unpriced_budget_cap_is_refused_by_name`** — A per-run budget cap the provisional price table cannot price is refused naming `maxBudget`: a cap that could never stop the run is not accepted (ADR-0074 D7, shared by ADR-0081).
  - Statement: `∀ {r : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Pi.Request} {grants : List AgentWorkspace.Authz.PathGrant.Grant}, r.policyReadable = true → AgentWorkspace.Authz.PathGrant.normaliseGrants (some AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Pi.protectedDirectory) r.grants = some grants → r.connectors = [] → r.budgetCap = true → AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Pi.priced (AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Pi.modelOf r) = false → AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Pi.compile r = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Pi.Outcome.refused (AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Refusal.capabilityUnsupported "maxBudget")`
  - Cites: `docs/formal/units/engine-pi.md#compile`, `packages/engine-pi/src/compile.ts#compilePiRun`, `packages/engine/src/prices.ts#provisionalPriceFor`
- **`Theorems.Normative.Pi.an_unspoken_protocol_is_refused_by_name`** — A connection served over any dialect but Anthropic Messages is refused naming `wireProtocols`.
  - Statement: `∀ {r : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Pi.Request} {grants : List AgentWorkspace.Authz.PathGrant.Grant} {b t w : String}, r.policyReadable = true → AgentWorkspace.Authz.PathGrant.normaliseGrants (some AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Pi.protectedDirectory) r.grants = some grants → r.connectors = [] → r.budgetCap = false → r.gateway = some (b, t, w) → w ≠ "anthropic-messages" → AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Pi.compile r = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Pi.Outcome.refused (AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.OpenAiAgents.Refusal.capabilityUnsupported "wireProtocols")`
  - Cites: `docs/formal/units/engine-pi.md#compile`, `packages/engine-pi/src/compile.ts#compilePiRun`
- **`Theorems.Normative.Pi.no_accepted_agent_has_a_connector`** — An accepted compile carries no connector: pi has no MCP client, so no agent with a connector is ever run on it.
  - Statement: `∀ {r : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Pi.Request} {c : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Pi.Compiled}, AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Pi.compile r = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Pi.Outcome.ok c → r.connectors = []`
  - Cites: `docs/formal/units/engine-pi.md#compile`, `packages/engine-pi/src/compile.ts#compilePiRun`
- **`Theorems.Normative.Pi.the_guard_blocks_bash_when_run_commands_is_off`** — Whenever the agent's `runCommands` switch is off, the compiled guard blocks every `bash` call, whatever it asks for: pi is never told about the tool, and a call the model invents is blocked.
  - Statement: `∀ {r : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Pi.Request} {c : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Pi.Compiled}, AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Pi.compile r = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Pi.Outcome.ok c → r.permissions.runCommands = false → ∀ (path : Option String), AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.Pi.guard c "bash" path = false`
  - Cites: `docs/formal/units/engine-pi.md#tools`, `packages/engine-pi/src/workspace.ts#piToolCallVerdict`, `packages/engine-pi/src/boundary.ts#startPiRun`

### T1 · PolicyCeiling

- **`Theorems.Normative.PolicyCeiling.policy_cannot_widen_iff_within`** — A write is refused exactly when it would widen: `policyWidenings` is empty if and only if every field of the configuration is within the ceiling.
  - Statement: `∀ (e : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.PolicyCeiling.Config) (c : Option AgentWorkspace.Concepts.PolicyCeiling.Ceiling), AgentWorkspace.Concepts.PolicyCeiling.violations e c = [] ↔ AgentWorkspace.Concepts.PolicyCeiling.within e c = true`
  - Cites: `docs/adr/0102-content-owners-edit-engineers-build-admins-narrow-stop-and-approve.md#slice-2-acceptance`, `packages/contracts/src/policy-ceiling.ts#policyWidenings`
- **`Theorems.Normative.PolicyCeiling.violations_name_each_field_once_in_key_order`** — The details name each field once, in C14's key order: the list has no repeats and is a sublist of the canonical order (permissions in `AGENT_PERMISSION_KEYS` order, the two limits, the engine, the model, then the distinct tools ascending).
  - Statement: `∀ (e : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.PolicyCeiling.Config) (c : Option AgentWorkspace.Concepts.PolicyCeiling.Ceiling), (AgentWorkspace.Concepts.PolicyCeiling.violations e c).Nodup ∧ (AgentWorkspace.Concepts.PolicyCeiling.violations e c).Sublist (AgentWorkspace.Concepts.PolicyCeiling.keyOrder e)`
  - Cites: `docs/adr/0102-content-owners-edit-engineers-build-admins-narrow-stop-and-approve.md#slice-2-acceptance`, `packages/contracts/src/policy-ceiling.ts#policyWidenings`

### T1 · Release

- **`Theorems.Normative.Release.promote_requires_gate`** — With a bar set, `promote … production` succeeds only if the promoted version's score is at least the bar; a version with no score is refused.
  - Statement: `∀ (b : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Release.Score) (r r' : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Release.Release) (a : AgentWorkspace.AgentId) (src : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Release.Env), AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Release.step (some b) r (AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Release.Op.promote a src AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Release.Env.production) = Except.ok r' → ∃ v s, r.pointer a src = some v ∧ r.evals a v = some s ∧ b ≤ s`
  - Cites: `docs/formal/domains/release.md#the-release-model`, `apps/web/server/agent-versions/release.ts#decidePromote`
- **`Theorems.Normative.Release.promote_without_a_bar_needs_no_evaluation`** — With no bar set, promotion needs no evaluation: whenever the source environment points at a version, promoting it to any environment succeeds and moves the target's pointer to it.
  - Statement: `∀ (r : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Release.Release) (a : AgentWorkspace.AgentId) (src dst : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Release.Env) (v : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Release.VersionNo), r.pointer a src = some v → AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Release.step none r (AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Release.Op.promote a src dst) = Except.ok (r.movePointer a dst v)`
  - Cites: `docs/formal/domains/release.md#the-release-model`, `apps/web/server/agent-versions/release.ts#decidePromote`

### T1 · RunCompose

- **`Theorems.Normative.RunCompose.environment_caller_overrides_a_default`** — A caller that sets a default itself keeps its value, and the default is not repeated.
  - Statement: `AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.RunCompose.compiledEnvironment [("ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH", "true")] "run" "session" "workspace" "/cwd/.claude" = some [("ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH", "true"), ("CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR", "/cwd/.claude"), ("CLAUDE_CODE_PROJECT_DIR_NAME", "workspace"), ("AGENT_WORKSPACE_RUN_ID", "run"), ("AGENT_WORKSPACE_SESSION_ID", "session")]`
  - Cites: `packages/engine-claude-agent-sdk/src/compile.ts#compileRunRequest`
- **`Theorems.Normative.RunCompose.environment_derives_scope_and_identity`** — Compiled subprocess variables include the adapter's defaults, the caller's values and four derived identity values.
  - Statement: `AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.RunCompose.compiledEnvironment [("CUSTOM", "value")] "run" "session" "workspace" "/cwd/.claude" = some [("ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH", "false"), ("CUSTOM", "value"), ("CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR", "/cwd/.claude"), ("CLAUDE_CODE_PROJECT_DIR_NAME", "workspace"), ("AGENT_WORKSPACE_RUN_ID", "run"), ("AGENT_WORKSPACE_SESSION_ID", "session")]`
  - Cites: `packages/engine-claude-agent-sdk/src/compile.ts#compileRunRequest`
- **`Theorems.Normative.RunCompose.environment_refuses_master_key_in_any_case`** — A mixed-case provider master-key variable prevents compilation.
  - Statement: `AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.RunCompose.compiledEnvironment [("Anthropic_Api_Key", "secret")] "r" "s" "w" "c" = none`
  - Cites: `packages/engine-claude-agent-sdk/src/compile.ts#compileRunRequest`
- **`Theorems.Normative.RunCompose.model_resolution_deployment_applies`** — With no other layer, a configured deployment default on a ready connection resolves at the deployment layer.
  - Statement: `AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.RunCompose.resolveModelForRun { deployment := some AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.RunCompose.readyDeployment✝ } = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.RunCompose.ModelResolution.ok AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.RunCompose.ModelLayer.deployment AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.RunCompose.readyChoice✝`
  - Cites: `apps/web/server/compose/run-request.ts#resolveModelForRun`
- **`Theorems.Normative.RunCompose.model_resolution_deployment_is_last`** — The deployment default is the last layer: a workspace default, or an agent selection, wins over it.
  - Statement: `AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.RunCompose.resolveModelForRun { workspace := some AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.RunCompose.readyChoice✝, deployment := some AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.RunCompose.readyDeployment✝ } = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.RunCompose.ModelResolution.ok AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.RunCompose.ModelLayer.workspace AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.RunCompose.readyChoice✝ ∧ AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.RunCompose.resolveModelForRun { agent := some AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.RunCompose.readyChoice✝, deployment := some AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.RunCompose.readyDeployment✝ } = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.RunCompose.ModelResolution.ok AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.RunCompose.ModelLayer.agent AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.RunCompose.readyChoice✝ ∧ AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.RunCompose.resolveModelForRun { project := some AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.RunCompose.readyChoice✝, deployment := some AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.RunCompose.readyDeployment✝ } = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.RunCompose.ModelResolution.ok AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.RunCompose.ModelLayer.project AgentWorkspace.Theorems.Normative.RunCompose.readyChoice✝`

## T2 — Invariants

### T2 · AgentFrames

- **`Theorems.Invariants.AgentFrames.a_row_serves_at_most_the_grammar_bound`** — **Every served id fits the documented grammar**: a row serves at most `maxFramesPerRow` frames, so a sub-index never needs a fourth digit, whatever a tenant's agent put in one turn.
  - Statement: `∀ (frames : List AgentWorkspace.Events.AgentFrames.Frame), (AgentWorkspace.Events.AgentFrames.capRowFrames frames).length ≤ AgentWorkspace.Events.AgentFrames.maxFramesPerRow ∧ (frames.length ≤ AgentWorkspace.Events.AgentFrames.maxFramesPerRow → AgentWorkspace.Events.AgentFrames.capRowFrames frames = frames)`
  - Cites: `apps/web/server/runs/agent-frames.ts#MAX_FRAMES_PER_ROW`
- **`Theorems.Invariants.AgentFrames.never_drops_an_engine_message`** — **Every classified engine message maps to at least one neutral frame.** There is no input for which `toAgentFrames` answers nothing: a message the neutral vocabulary cannot express becomes `agent.native`, and one that could not be parsed becomes `agent.malformed`. This is the guarantee the runner's writer relies on without re-checking, and the reason the closed frame set is safe to close.
  - Statement: `∀ (classified : AgentWorkspace.Events.AgentFrames.Classified), AgentWorkspace.Events.AgentFrames.toAgentFrames classified ≠ []`
  - Cites: `docs/sdk/04-api-specification.md#63-the-neutral-event-vocabulary`, `packages/run-protocol/src/schemas.ts#toAgentFrames`
- **`Theorems.Invariants.AgentFrames.no_tool_frames_from_another_role`** — A turn that is neither the assistant's nor the user's carries no tool frame at all.
  - Statement: `∀ (items : List AgentWorkspace.JValue), AgentWorkspace.Events.AgentFrames.toolFrames "system" (some (AgentWorkspace.JValue.arr items)) = []`
  - Cites: `packages/run-protocol/src/schemas.ts#toAgentFrames`
- **`Theorems.Invariants.AgentFrames.resume_serves_a_different_row_whole`** — A cursor naming another row's sequence serves that row whole: a cursor into a row the store can no longer retain has already produced a `stream-reset`, and the oldest retained row is then new to the client in its entirety.
  - Statement: `∀ {α : Type} (cursorSequence i sequence : Nat) (subIndexed : Bool) (served : List α), ¬cursorSequence = sequence → AgentWorkspace.Events.AgentFrames.resumeWithinRow (some (cursorSequence, i)) sequence subIndexed served = served`
  - Cites: `apps/web/server/runs/agent-frames.ts#upgradeEventStream`
- **`Theorems.Invariants.AgentFrames.resume_serves_a_one_to_one_row_whole`** — A sub-indexed cursor naming a row that was served **one-to-one** serves that row whole. The server never writes such an id — only an upgraded legacy row is served in parts — so the cursor is stale or forged; the row is delivered rather than dropped on the strength of a position it does not have, the same "reported, not guessed" answer the rest of the read path gives.
  - Statement: `∀ {α : Type} (sequence i : Nat) (served : List α), AgentWorkspace.Events.AgentFrames.resumeWithinRow (some (sequence, i)) sequence false served = served`
  - Cites: `apps/web/server/runs/agent-frames.ts#upgradeEventStream`
- **`Theorems.Invariants.AgentFrames.resume_within_row_loses_and_repeats_nothing`** — **Resuming inside a row neither loses a frame nor repeats one.** A client that last saw `<sequence>.<i>` is re-served that whole row — the store seeks by row and cannot deliver half of one — and given only the frames after `i`. Concatenating what it already had with what it is served back reconstructs the row exactly once.
  - Statement: `∀ {α : Type} (sequence i : Nat) (served : List α), List.take (i + 1) served ++ AgentWorkspace.Events.AgentFrames.resumeWithinRow (some (sequence, i)) sequence true served = served`
  - Cites: `docs/sdk/site/guides/streaming.mdx#resuming-with-after-and-last-event-id`, `apps/web/server/runs/agent-frames.ts#upgradeEventStream`
- **`Theorems.Invariants.AgentFrames.row_positions_are_a_range`** — The positions a row's frames are served under are `0, 1, …`, so the ids inside one row are strictly increasing by construction.
  - Statement: `∀ {α : Type} (xs : List α), List.map Prod.fst (AgentWorkspace.Events.AgentFrames.indexed xs) = List.range xs.length`
  - Cites: `apps/web/server/runs/agent-frames.ts#wireEventId`
- **`Theorems.Invariants.AgentFrames.served_frames_keep_emission_order`** — **A row's frames are served in the order the mapping emitted them, under ascending ids.** The served frames are exactly the frames `toAgentFrames` produced (capped at the grammar's bound), in its order; the sub-indices are `0, 1, …` in that same order; and the ids are strictly increasing. This is the general form of `engine_message_fans_out_in_order`.
  - Statement: `∀ (systemSubtypes resultSubtypes eventTypes : List String) (sequence : Nat) (data : AgentWorkspace.JValue), List.map Prod.snd (AgentWorkspace.Events.AgentFrames.serveLegacyRow systemSubtypes resultSubtypes eventTypes sequence data) = AgentWorkspace.Events.AgentFrames.capRowFrames (AgentWorkspace.Events.AgentFrames.upgradeLegacy systemSubtypes resultSubtypes eventTypes data) ∧ List.map Prod.fst (AgentWorkspace.Events.AgentFrames.serveLegacyRow systemSubtypes resultSubtypes eventTypes sequence data) = List.map (fun i => (sequence, some i)) (List.range (AgentWorkspace.Events.AgentFrames.capRowFrames (AgentWorkspace.Events.AgentFrames.upgradeLegacy systemSubtypes resultSubtypes eventTypes data)).length) ∧ AgentWorkspace.Events.AgentFrames.idsIncreasing (List.map Prod.fst (AgentWorkspace.Events.AgentFrames.serveLegacyRow systemSubtypes resultSubtypes eventTypes sequence data)) = true`
  - Cites: `apps/web/server/runs/agent-frames.ts#upgradeStoredEvent`, `apps/web/server/runs/agent-frames.ts#wireEventId`
- **`Theorems.Invariants.AgentFrames.tool_frames_follow_the_turn_that_can_carry_them`** — **A call frame can only come from an assistant turn, and a result frame only from a user turn.** This is what makes the pairing invariant hold across a whole run without the mapping remembering anything: the Claude Agent SDK carries a `tool_use` block on the assistant's message and the matching `tool_result` on the *following* user message, so the frame announcing a `toolCallId` is always emitted before the frame answering it.
  - Statement: `∀ (items : List AgentWorkspace.JValue), (AgentWorkspace.Events.AgentFrames.toolFrames "assistant" (some (AgentWorkspace.JValue.arr items))).all AgentWorkspace.Events.AgentFrames.Frame.isToolCall = true ∧ (AgentWorkspace.Events.AgentFrames.toolFrames "user" (some (AgentWorkspace.JValue.arr items))).all AgentWorkspace.Events.AgentFrames.Frame.isToolResult = true`
  - Cites: `docs/sdk/04-api-specification.md#63-the-neutral-event-vocabulary`, `packages/run-protocol/src/schemas.ts#toAgentFrames`
- **`Theorems.Invariants.AgentFrames.unmapped_message_is_carried_natively`** — The fallback of an unmapped message names the engine's own message, so nothing is lost when the neutral vocabulary has nothing to say about it.
  - Statement: `∀ (classified : AgentWorkspace.Events.AgentFrames.Classified), AgentWorkspace.Events.AgentFrames.mappedFrames classified = [] → AgentWorkspace.Events.AgentFrames.toAgentFrames classified = [AgentWorkspace.Events.AgentFrames.fallbackFrame classified]`
  - Cites: `packages/run-protocol/src/schemas.ts#toAgentFrames`
- **`Theorems.Invariants.AgentFrames.wire_ids_follow_the_documented_grammar`** — And the ids are rendered under the documented grammar.
  - Statement: `AgentWorkspace.Events.AgentFrames.wireEventId 41 none = "41" ∧ AgentWorkspace.Events.AgentFrames.wireEventId 41 (some 0) = "41.0" ∧ AgentWorkspace.Events.AgentFrames.wireEventId 41 (some 7) = "41.7"`
  - Cites: `apps/web/server/runs/agent-frames.ts#wireEventId`

### T2 · AuthzDecide

- **`Theorems.Invariants.AuthzDecide.every_allow_is_backed_by_the_table`** — Every `allow` that consulted §21's table is backed by it: the role parses, the path parses to the allowed resource, the grant is that role's cell, it is not `none`, an `own` grant saw an `own` or `not-applicable` fact, and a `permitted` grant saw an `own` or `permitted` fact (ADR-0152).
  - Statement: `∀ (q : AgentWorkspace.Authz.Decide.Query) (f : AgentWorkspace.Authz.Decide.RouteFacts), AgentWorkspace.Authz.Decide.decideOrdinary q = AgentWorkspace.Authz.Decide.Decision.allow (some f) → ∃ role sub id op, AgentWorkspace.Authz.Roles.parseRoleInput q.role = some role ∧ AgentWorkspace.Authz.Decide.parsePath q.path = AgentWorkspace.Authz.Decide.ParsedPath.ok f.resource sub id ∧ f.operation = AgentWorkspace.Authz.Decide.RouteOperation.ofOperation op ∧ f.grant = AgentWorkspace.Authz.Permissions.grantFor role f.resource op ∧ f.grant ≠ AgentWorkspace.Authz.Permissions.Grant.none ∧ (f.grant = AgentWorkspace.Authz.Permissions.Grant.own → q.ownership = AgentWorkspace.Authz.Decide.Ownership.own ∨ q.ownership = AgentWorkspace.Authz.Decide.Ownership.notApplicable) ∧ (f.grant = AgentWorkspace.Authz.Permissions.Grant.permitted → q.ownership = AgentWorkspace.Authz.Decide.Ownership.own ∨ q.ownership = AgentWorkspace.Authz.Decide.Ownership.permitted)`
  - Cites: `docs/sdk/04-api-specification.md#33-roles`, `docs/adr/W9-AUTH-117-viewer-permitted-agent-grants.md#decision`, `apps/web/server/rbac/decide.ts#decide`
- **`Theorems.Invariants.AuthzDecide.scope_only_narrows`** — A browser-token scope only narrows: the scoped decision is the unscoped one, or a `token_out_of_scope` deny — never an `allow` the minter would not get, and never a different refusal.

### T2 · AuthzTenancy

- **`Theorems.Invariants.AuthzTenancy.object_keys_carry_their_workspace`** — Every backend key or prefix a scoped object-store call reaches begins with the two segments `workspaces` and the store's workspace id, whenever that id is a single segment (always, under the target acceptance rule; for today's rule, whenever the id has no `/`).
  - Statement: `∀ (acceptWs : String → Bool) (ws : String) (op : AgentWorkspace.Authz.Tenancy.ObjectOp), ws.toList.contains '/' = false → ∀ {ks : List String}, AgentWorkspace.Authz.Tenancy.scopedObjectOp acceptWs ws op = AgentWorkspace.Authz.Tenancy.ObjectOutcome.backend ks → ∀ (k : String), k ∈ ks → ∃ R, AgentWorkspace.Authz.Surface.splitSlash k.toList = "workspaces".toList :: ws.toList :: R`
  - Cites: `docs/adr/W2-CP-03-object-key-safety.md#decision`, `packages/core/src/storage/object-store.ts#createScopedObjectStore`
- **`Theorems.Invariants.AuthzTenancy.object_keys_of_two_workspaces_are_disjoint`** — Under the target acceptance rule, no key or listing prefix of one workspace's object store is a key of another workspace's, nor a segment prefix of one: a key of workspace A is never a key of workspace B, and listing A never lists B.
  - Statement: `∀ (ws₁ ws₂ : String), ws₁ ≠ ws₂ → ∀ (op₁ op₂ : AgentWorkspace.Authz.Tenancy.ObjectOp) {ks₁ ks₂ : List String}, AgentWorkspace.Authz.Tenancy.scopedObjectOpTarget ws₁ op₁ = AgentWorkspace.Authz.Tenancy.ObjectOutcome.backend ks₁ → AgentWorkspace.Authz.Tenancy.scopedObjectOpTarget ws₂ op₂ = AgentWorkspace.Authz.Tenancy.ObjectOutcome.backend ks₂ → ∀ {k₁ k₂ : String}, k₁ ∈ ks₁ → k₂ ∈ ks₂ → k₁ ≠ k₂ ∧ ¬AgentWorkspace.Authz.Surface.splitSlash k₁.toList <+: AgentWorkspace.Authz.Surface.splitSlash k₂.toList`
  - Cites: `docs/adr/W2-CP-03-object-key-safety.md#decision`, `packages/core/src/storage/object-store.ts#createScopedObjectStore`
- **`Theorems.Invariants.AuthzTenancy.principal_by_id_reads_only_its_workspace`** — `principalById(ws, pid)` builds its record only from rows of workspace `ws`: a membership principal's role comes from a membership of `ws` (and its label from that membership's user), an API-key principal's role and label from a key of `ws` that is neither revoked nor expired at `now`.
  - Statement: `∀ (st : AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.State) (ws pid : String) (now : Nat) (rec : AgentWorkspace.Authz.Tenancy.DirectoryRecord), AgentWorkspace.Authz.Tenancy.principalById st ws pid now = some rec → rec.workspaceId = ws ∧ (rec.kind = AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Principal.Kind.membership → ∃ m, m ∈ st AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.TableName.memberships ∧ m.get "workspace_id" = some ws ∧ m.get "role" = some rec.role ∧ m.get "user_id" = rec.userId ∧ ∃ u, u ∈ st AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.TableName.users ∧ u.get "id" = rec.userId ∧ u.get "name" = some rec.label) ∧ (rec.kind = AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Principal.Kind.apiKey → ∃ k, k ∈ st AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.TableName.apiKeys ∧ k.get "workspace_id" = some ws ∧ k.get "id" = rec.apiKeyId ∧ k.get "role" = some rec.role ∧ k.get "name" = some rec.label ∧ k.get "revoked_at" = none ∧ ((k.get "expires_at").isNone = true ∨ AgentWorkspace.Authz.Tenancy.after (k.get "expires_at") now = true))`
  - Cites: `docs/sdk/04-api-specification.md#311-browser-tokens-issue-236-sdk-04-s-1`, `packages/core/src/db/repositories/directory.ts#principalById`
- **`Theorems.Invariants.AuthzTenancy.repository_write_touches_only_its_workspace`** — A repository write bound to scope `s` on a tenant-scoped table, once PostgreSQL commits or rolls it back, leaves every row that is not of `s`'s workspace — every other tenant's rows and every global row — exactly as it was: no scoped operation reaches another workspace.
  - Statement: `∀ (st : AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.State) (s : AgentWorkspace.Authz.Tenancy.WorkspaceScope) (w : AgentWorkspace.Authz.Tenancy.RepoWrite), AgentWorkspace.Authz.Tenancy.isScopedTable w.table = true → ∀ (u : AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.TableName) {r : AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.Row}, AgentWorkspace.Authz.Tenancy.rowTenant u r ≠ some s.workspaceId → (r ∈ AgentWorkspace.Authz.Tenancy.repoCommit st s w u ↔ r ∈ st u)`
  - Cites: `docs/adr/W2-DB-02-the-repository-shape.md#decision`, `packages/core/src/db/repositories/scope.ts#requireWorkspaceScope`
- **`Theorems.Invariants.AuthzTenancy.scoped_select_reads_only_its_workspace`** — A scoped read returns only rows whose workspace is the scope's.
  - Statement: `∀ (st : AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.State) (s : AgentWorkspace.Authz.Tenancy.WorkspaceScope) (t : AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.TableName) (p : AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.Row → Bool) {r : AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.Row}, r ∈ AgentWorkspace.Authz.Tenancy.scopedSelect st s t p → AgentWorkspace.Authz.Tenancy.rowTenant t r = some s.workspaceId`
  - Cites: `docs/adr/W2-DB-02-the-repository-shape.md#decision`, `packages/core/src/db/repositories/scope.ts#WorkspaceScope`

### T2 · BehaviourEngines

- **`Theorems.Invariants.BehaviourEngines.a_run_never_claims_an_engine_session_id`** — A run never writes an engine session id either: the identity is recorded only after the runner reports one, by {@link recordIdentity}.

- **`Theorems.Invariants.BehaviourEngines.a_run_never_repins_the_session`** — No run ever re-pins its session, whatever it asks for. Switching a live session to another engine is a non-goal of the engine programme: the session's history belongs to the engine that produced it, so a run that cannot join it is refused rather than allowed to take it over.
  - Statement: `∀ (agentEngine : String) (s : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.LaunchState), (AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.startRun agentEngine s).snd.sessionEngine = s.sessionEngine`
  - Cites: `docs/adr/0065-an-agents-engine-is-an-extension-point-behind-one-port.md#d8--a-session-is-pinned-to-one-engine`, `apps/web/server/runs/api.ts#startRun`
- **`Theorems.Invariants.BehaviourEngines.a_run_preserves_the_pairing`** — A fresh session satisfies the pairing, and a run does not break it: a run writes neither cell.
  - Statement: `∀ (agentEngine : String) (s : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.LaunchState), AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.launchPaired s = true → AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.launchPaired (AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.startRun agentEngine s).snd = true`
  - Cites: `packages/core/src/db/schema/sessions.ts#sessions`
- **`Theorems.Invariants.BehaviourEngines.a_run_records_the_engine_the_session_is_pinned_to`** — A run in a session pinned to a **published** engine records that engine, and appends exactly one row. The hypothesis is the code's, not a convenience: `pinSessionEngine` narrows the engine it records with `publishedEngineId`, which throws — and so writes no row — for an id outside `ENGINE_IDS` (`apps/web/server/runs/api.test.ts`, "refuses to record a run for an engine the contracts do not publish"). `startRun` below models the published case only.
  - Statement: `∀ (engine : String) (engineSessionId : Option String) (runs : List AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.RunRow), engine ∈ AgentWorkspace.Contracts.Engines.engineIds → AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.startRun engine { sessionEngine := some engine, engineSessionId := engineSessionId, runs := runs } = (AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.LaunchVerdict.created engine, { sessionEngine := some engine, engineSessionId := engineSessionId, runs := runs ++ [{ engine := engine }] })`
  - Cites: `apps/web/server/runs/api.ts#startRun`
- **`Theorems.Invariants.BehaviourEngines.an_unpinned_session_accepts_any_engine`** — A session no run has pinned accepts any **published** engine, and records the agent's own. This is what makes `sessions.engine` NULL a real state rather than a missing value: a project session created before its first run is launched, not refused. "Any" is every id the contracts publish, not every string: `pinSessionEngine` narrows the agent's engine with `publishedEngineId` before it can be recorded, and that throws, writing no row, for an id outside `ENGINE_IDS`. The refusal theorems above need no such hypothesis, because a refusal and a throw both leave the rows as they were.
  - Statement: `∀ (agentEngine : String) (engineSessionId : Option String) (runs : List AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.RunRow), agentEngine ∈ AgentWorkspace.Contracts.Engines.engineIds → AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.startRun agentEngine { sessionEngine := none, engineSessionId := engineSessionId, runs := runs } = (AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.LaunchVerdict.created agentEngine, { sessionEngine := none, engineSessionId := engineSessionId, runs := runs ++ [{ engine := agentEngine }] })`
  - Cites: `apps/web/server/engines/session-engine.ts#pinSessionEngine`
- **`Theorems.Invariants.BehaviourEngines.recording_identity_establishes_the_pairing`** — Recording a reported identity pins the engine and the id together, so the pairing invariant holds of the state it produces from **any** prior state. Migration 0025 closes the same gap for rows written before this code.
  - Statement: `∀ (engine reported : String) (s : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.LaunchState), AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.launchPaired (AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.recordIdentity engine reported s) = true`
  - Cites: `apps/web/server/composition/session-launch.ts#recordReportedSessionIdentity`
- **`Theorems.Invariants.BehaviourEngines.session_engine_mismatch_creates_no_run`** — A run whose agent's engine differs from `sessions.engine` is refused, and the state is **unchanged**: no run row is created, not created-and-rolled-back.
  - Statement: `∀ (agentEngine : String) (s : AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.LaunchState), (AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.startRun agentEngine s).fst = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.LaunchVerdict.engineMismatch → (AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.startRun agentEngine s).snd = s`
  - Cites: `docs/adr/0065-an-agents-engine-is-an-extension-point-behind-one-port.md#d8--a-session-is-pinned-to-one-engine`, `apps/web/server/runs/api.ts#startRun`
- **`Theorems.Invariants.BehaviourEngines.session_engine_mismatch_is_a_four_oh_nine`** — The refusal travels as `409 session_engine_mismatch`, apart from `session_not_usable`: the request is well formed, and the session has a history this run does not belong to.
  - Statement: `AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.LaunchVerdict.engineMismatch.code = some "session_engine_mismatch" ∧ AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.LaunchVerdict.engineMismatch.status = 409`
  - Cites: `packages/contracts/src/engines.ts#ENGINE_PROBLEM_CODES`
- **`Theorems.Invariants.BehaviourEngines.session_engine_mismatch_is_exactly_a_different_pin`** — The refusal happens **exactly** when the session is pinned to another engine: a session pinned to the agent's own engine is never refused, and one pinned to any other engine always is.
  - Statement: `∀ (agentEngine pinned : String) (engineSessionId : Option String) (runs : List AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.RunRow), (AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.startRun agentEngine { sessionEngine := some pinned, engineSessionId := engineSessionId, runs := runs }).fst = AgentWorkspace.Behaviour.Engines.LaunchVerdict.engineMismatch ↔ pinned ≠ agentEngine`
  - Cites: `apps/web/server/engines/session-engine.ts#pinSessionEngine`

- **`Theorems.Invariants.ConceptCatalog.created_connector_meets_the_shape_checks`** — "Validating here means the database's constraints are a backstop": every body `parseCreateConnectorBody` accepts yields a row that passes the six shape checks of `mcp_servers` (command xor URL by transport, arguments only for `stdio`, a non-blank command, an absolute `http(s)` URL, and a credential secret exactly when the authentication type needs one).
  - Statement: `∀ (b : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Connector.Body) (p : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Connector.Parsed), AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Connector.parseBody (some b) = Except.ok p → ∀ (id : AgentWorkspace.ConnectorId) (ws : AgentWorkspace.WorkspaceId) (sid : AgentWorkspace.SecretId) (createdBy : Option AgentWorkspace.UserId) (owner : AgentWorkspace.PrincipalId), (p.toConnector id ws sid createdBy owner).stdioHasCommand = true ∧ (p.toConnector id ws sid createdBy owner).remoteHasUrl = true ∧ (p.toConnector id ws sid createdBy owner).argsStdioOnly = true ∧ (p.toConnector id ws sid createdBy owner).commandNotBlank = true ∧ (p.toConnector id ws sid createdBy owner).urlShapeOk = true ∧ (p.toConnector id ws sid createdBy owner).credentialRequired = true`
  - Cites: `docs/sdk/04-api-specification.md#58-connectors-mcp-servers--awconnectors`, `apps/web/server/connectors/contract.ts#parseCreateConnectorBody`
- **`Theorems.Invariants.ConceptCatalog.delete_by_prefix_keeps_exactly_the_other_rows`** — A subtree delete keeps exactly the rows outside the prefix.
  - Statement: `∀ (pre : String) (fs : List AgentWorkspace.Concepts.File.File) (f : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.File.File), f ∈ AgentWorkspace.Concepts.File.deleteByPrefix pre fs ↔ f ∈ fs ∧ AgentWorkspace.Concepts.File.underPrefix pre f.path = false`
  - Cites: `packages/core/src/db/repositories/resource-catalogs.ts#pathUnderPrefix`
- **`Theorems.Invariants.ConceptCatalog.delete_file_removes_exactly_that_path`** — Deleting one file (`deleteFile`) removes exactly the row at that path; unlike a subtree delete, the rows under a folder's path stay.
  - Statement: `∀ (path : String) (fs : List AgentWorkspace.Concepts.File.File) (f : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.File.File), f ∈ AgentWorkspace.Concepts.File.deleteFile path fs ↔ f ∈ fs ∧ f.path ≠ path`
  - Cites: `packages/core/src/db/repositories/resource-catalogs.ts#createDatabaseResourceCatalogRepositoryProvider`
- **`Theorems.Invariants.ConceptCatalog.delete_skill_removes_exactly_that_name`** — Deleting one skill (`deleteSkill`) removes exactly the row with that name.
  - Statement: `∀ (name : String) (ss : List AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Skill.Skill) (s : AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Skill.Skill), s ∈ AgentWorkspace.Concepts.Skill.deleteSkill name ss ↔ s ∈ ss ∧ s.name ≠ name`

  - Statement: `∀ (st : AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.State), AgentWorkspace.Er.Current.Catalog.consistent st = true → ∀ {r r' : AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.Row}, AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.References AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.catalogue st AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.TableName.projectMcpServers (AgentWorkspace.Er.Current.Catalog.fk AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.TableName.projectMcpServers "project_mcp_servers_server_workspace_fk") r r' → AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.tenantOf AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.catalogue AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.TableName.projectMcpServers r = AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.tenantOf AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.catalogue (AgentWorkspace.Er.Current.Catalog.fk AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.TableName.projectMcpServers "project_mcp_servers_server_workspace_fk").refTable r'`

- **`Theorems.Invariants.ConceptCatalog.project_mcp_servers_server_workspace_fk_names_exactly_one_parent`** — In every consistent state, every `project_mcp_servers` row names exactly one `mcp_servers` row through `project_mcp_servers_server_workspace_fk` (its columns are `NOT NULL`).
  - Statement: `∀ (st : AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.State), AgentWorkspace.Er.Current.Catalog.consistent st = true → ∀ {r : AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.Row}, r ∈ st AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.TableName.projectMcpServers → ∃ r', r' ∈ st (AgentWorkspace.Er.Current.Catalog.fk AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.TableName.projectMcpServers "project_mcp_servers_server_workspace_fk").refTable ∧ r'.project (AgentWorkspace.Er.Current.Catalog.fk AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.TableName.projectMcpServers "project_mcp_servers_server_workspace_fk").refColumns = r.project (AgentWorkspace.Er.Current.Catalog.fk AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.TableName.projectMcpServers "project_mcp_servers_server_workspace_fk").columns ∧ ∀ (r'' : AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.Row), r'' ∈ st (AgentWorkspace.Er.Current.Catalog.fk AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.TableName.projectMcpServers "project_mcp_servers_server_workspace_fk").refTable → r''.project (AgentWorkspace.Er.Current.Catalog.fk AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.TableName.projectMcpServers "project_mcp_servers_server_workspace_fk").refColumns = r.project (AgentWorkspace.Er.Current.Catalog.fk AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.TableName.projectMcpServers "project_mcp_servers_server_workspace_fk").columns → r'' = r'`

- **`Theorems.Invariants.ConceptCatalog.project_mcp_servers_workspace_id_workspaces_id_fk_joins_one_workspace`** — In every consistent state, a `project_mcp_servers` row and the `workspaces` row it references through `project_mcp_servers_workspace_id_workspaces_id_fk` belong to the same workspace.

- **`Theorems.Invariants.ConceptCatalog.project_mcp_servers_workspace_id_workspaces_id_fk_names_exactly_one_parent`** — In every consistent state, every `project_mcp_servers` row names exactly one `workspaces` row through `project_mcp_servers_workspace_id_workspaces_id_fk` (its columns are `NOT NULL`).
  - Statement: `∀ (st : AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.State), AgentWorkspace.Er.Current.Catalog.consistent st = true → ∀ {r : AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.Row}, r ∈ st AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.TableName.projectMcpServers → ∃ r', r' ∈ st (AgentWorkspace.Er.Current.Catalog.fk AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.TableName.projectMcpServers "project_mcp_servers_workspace_id_workspaces_id_fk").refTable ∧ r'.project (AgentWorkspace.Er.Current.Catalog.fk AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.TableName.projectMcpServers "project_mcp_servers_workspace_id_workspaces_id_fk").refColumns = r.project (AgentWorkspace.Er.Current.Catalog.fk AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.TableName.projectMcpServers "project_mcp_servers_workspace_id_workspaces_id_fk").columns ∧ ∀ (r'' : AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.Row), r'' ∈ st (AgentWorkspace.Er.Current.Catalog.fk AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.TableName.projectMcpServers "project_mcp_servers_workspace_id_workspaces_id_fk").refTable → r''.project (AgentWorkspace.Er.Current.Catalog.fk AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.TableName.projectMcpServers "project_mcp_servers_workspace_id_workspaces_id_fk").refColumns = r.project (AgentWorkspace.Er.Current.Catalog.fk AgentWorkspace.Er.Core.TableName.projectMcpServers "project_mcp_servers_workspace_id_workspaces_id_fk").columns → r'' = r'`
